business_problem: ABB wanted to give employees a safe, responsible way to use generative AI in daily work so they could improve productivity, explore ideas more effectively, and support ongoing learning and career development.
solution_summary: ABB built and rolled out Abby, an in-house generative AI assistant for employees, alongside a broader enablement program focused on safe and responsible AI use. Abby is integrated with ABB's internal libraries and systems so staff can retrieve company-specific information, and it also lets them search public information for broader research. Employees submit prompts in Abby for daily tasks such as content creation, data analysis, and web research, and the tool routes those requests to one of more than 15 supported large language models based on user needs. Abby also serves outputs back into employee workflows by generating presentations with ABB templates and by allowing users to create custom task agents that automate repetitive work. Training, approved-tool guidance, and internal resources act as the governance layer around adoption.

business_outcome: ABB reports that the program increased employee access to generative AI tools and training, enabling productivity, exploration, and self-development at scale across the workforce.
